_README: C123/C124 decision ledger for the Open House funnel. The weekly report reads this file from main and renders it as the timeline and the hypothesis board; the recommendation engine skips any move still inside its measure window. APPEND ONLY: never delete or rewrite an entry. To change direction, add a 'retraction' or 'pivot' entry that names the id it supersedes in 'supersedes'. Kinds: decision, pivot, build, measurement, correction, retraction, hypothesis. Hypothesis 'test' is graded every week against the snapshot: metric is a key in targets.js (rates), op '>=' or '<=', value in percent. Times are Central.

entries.title: Round 11 opens: an ad visitor's first win is the goal
entries.detail: The paid-ad funnel is judged by one thing: does a stranger from an ad reach a first win (the welcome video and its Quick check) on the platform?

entries.title: C118: Ali's 109-second avatar welcome video replaces the program video
entries.detail: Self-hosted, first assignment for every Explorer who had not finished it (804 learners), with a Quick check rewritten from its transcript.

entries.title: The avatar video gets at least 20% of the people who press play to watch 75%
entries.detail: Baseline with the old YouTube video: 7 of 51 brand-new sign-ups finished (14%). First 27.8 hours with the new one: 2 of 10 (20%), too few to call. 8 of the 9 who quit left within 18 seconds.

entries.title: C119: the player records exactly where a learner leaves the video
entries.detail: Closing the tab now sends a final watch beat. Proven on production: a tab closed at 8.3 seconds recorded 8 seconds. Before this, a quit under 15 seconds left no trace.

entries.title: The landing page now promotes the Open House; the account is created by the Open House sign-up
entries.detail: Ali's call. Visitors save a seat at the live Open House, and that one form also creates their $0 account and sends a welcome email pointing at the video. Every number in this report starts here.

entries.title: Asking for an Open House seat converts at least 20% of landing page visitors
C120: the Open House funnel tested end to end, with a rerunnable step report
entries.detail: A test sign-up passed every step on production. The real numbers showed the leak: 5 sign-ups, 5 accounts, 5 welcome emails, 0 people entered. The welcome email lands in Gmail's Updates tab.

entries.title: C121: an Access your account button signs a new sign-up straight in
entries.detail: Ali's idea: skip the trip to the inbox. The email stays as the way back. An address that already has an account is told to sign in.

entries.title: With the button, at least 70% of brand-new accounts go in
entries.detail: Before the button: 0 of 5. Note that this week's window still includes sign-ups from before 7:20 AM on 11 Nov, who never saw the button.

entries.title: C123: a weekly report follows every person through every fork
entries.detail: First edition: 53 visitors, 14 sign-ups, 13 new accounts, 4 entered (all by the button), 0 pressed play. Facebook converted 40.7% of its visitors, Instagram 9.1%.

entries.title: "Finished the video" now means watched 75%, and collecting the credit is its own step
entries.detail: C120 and the first C123 edition counted a finish only when the credit was collected. A learner who watched 97% and never clicked showed as not finishing. Both numbers are now shown.

entries.title: Once the page makes play the obvious next step on a phone, at least half of the people who reach the welcome video press play
entries.detail: 4 brand-new accounts, all on phones, opened the welcome video card within 4 seconds of signing up and sent no watch beat at all. A later phone learner played to 97% and was recorded, so phone beats work: these 4 most likely never pressed play.

entries.title: C124: one starred move a week, emailed Wednesdays 8 AM CT to Taiwo, Sohail and Ali
entries.detail: The report now names the single move with the greatest impact and attaches a prompt that makes it. Every move made is added to this ledger with the hypothesis it tests, so the next report grades it.

entries.title: Collecting the credit runs at 88.4% across all 43 learners who earned it, not the 67% a three-person week suggested
entries.detail: The 12 Nov edition starred "1 watched 75%+ and never collected the credit" and graded the step at 66.7% (2 of 3). Measured across every learner with progress on the welcome video: 43 have watched 75%+, 38 collected, 5 did not - 88.4% against the 90% target, so the step is close to target and the weekly figure was small-sample noise. Of the 5, four never signed in again after crossing the threshold, so they left mid-session rather than being refused; the credit stays collectable because watchVerdictFor reads the stored watch state and returns met=true whenever they return. Exactly one crossed 100% and signed in again 14 minutes later without collecting, which is the only real signal here and is n=1. Also worth saying plainly: 0 learners hold the credit with under 75% watched, so the gate is sound, and the insight wording "the platform did not count it" overstates a deliberate design - 75% unlocks the button and the click awards the points.
